the development of a process-based model that can be used to predict the impact of rainfall events on the soil and salt load of surface waters.
the development and application of process-based modeling to estimate the effects of land management on soil and salt load in the UCRB and other arid and semiarid regions of the world.

the new parameter estimation equations developed in this study can be used for improved predictions of soil loss and runoff salt load in the upper Colorado River Basin.
we have developed a process-based model that can be used to predict soil and salt loss from rangelands.
the RHEM model can predict runoff, soil loss, and salt load with good precision on saline and sodic soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil sodicity should be accounted for in estimating sheet and splash erosion, and this will improve the accuracy of soil loss predictions.
RHEM can be used to predict salt load from rainfall-driven runoff on saline and sodic soils.
